title: Deploy synthetic ingest & query probes to validate analytics SLIs across tenants
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Goal: Add a lightweight synthetic probe layer that exercises the analytics ingest and query paths end-to-end across a representative set of tenants. The probe should continuously validate the SLIs we publish for analytics pipelines (ingest success rate, end-to-end processing latency, query freshness) and surface regressions to the Console and PagerDuty. Scope includes probe design, probe runner infra, tagging/trace propagation, dashboards, and automated alerts.

Why: We have gaps in our ability to detect regressions that only appear under realistic multi-tenant request shapes (small bursts, long tails, sparse tenants). Real customer traffic is ideal but slow to surface regressions and missing coverage for rare edge cases. Synthetic probes give deterministic coverage for SLO verification, release gating, and root-cause repros.

Out of scope: billing changes to exclude synthetic traffic (handled by finance), deep model-serving probes (separate ENG ticket), and long-term storage of synthetic payloads beyond 14 days.
acceptance_criteria: A probe runner exists that can emit ingest traffic and query traffic against the analytics pipeline using a configurable tenant mix and request rate
Synthetic requests are tagged (header 'X-Synthetic-Probe: true') and trace context is propagated end-to-end so traces surface in the observability stack
Defined SLIs evaluate probe traffic separately and are visible on a dedicated 'Synthetic Probes' dashboard for p50/p95/p99 latency and success rate
Automated alerts trigger when probe-derived SLIs fall below thresholds (ingest_success_rate < 99.5% over 5m or end_to_end_p95 > 2s for ingest-to-dashboards), with runbook link attached
Probe runs are non-destructive and do not modify customer data; all synthetic payloads are isolated and scrubbed
Documentation and runbook created with steps to run targeted repros and to mute probes during known maintenance windows
tasks: Design probe payloads and tenant mix matrix (small, medium, large tenants; cold vs warm cache)
Implement probe runner as Kubernetes CronJob + API to trigger ad-hoc runs
Add tracer propagation and tag header to gateway & ingest services; update telemetry to mark synthetic traces
Create 'Synthetic Probes' Grafana dashboard with slis, waterfall traces, and tenant distribution heatmap
Wire alerts in alertmanager with annotations pointing to runbook and responsible on-call team
Add feature flag to enable/disable probes per environment (prod, staging, canary)
Create Confluence runbook and link to ticket/artifacts
progress_updates: 2026-02-12: Kickoff meeting with analytics, infra, and platform observability. Agreed scope and SLA thresholds; infra to provide k8s namespace for probe runners.
2026-02-18: Payload matrix drafted — includes 3 tenant classes and two access patterns (burst vs steady). Shared in #analytics-observability for feedback.

2026-02-24: Prototype probe runner implemented as a lightweight Go binary. Emits batched events to the ingest gateway and attaches 'X-Synthetic-Probe' header. Initial runs executed against staging pipeline; traces appear in Jaeger.
2026-03-03: Added trace context propagation fixes — discovered that async worker was dropping traceparent on retry; patched in PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/analytics/pull/874
2026-03-08: Dashboard first draft landed: https://grafana.redwood.io/d/analytics/synthetic-probes. Missing tenant heatmap and alert rules (in progress).
2026-03-12: Alerting rules proposed in alertmanager PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/482. Pending review from SRE and on-call owners. Moved ticket to In Progress.
Blockers: Need an agreed policy for synthetic request retention and scrubbing (privacy). Ops/legal loop-in scheduled 2026-03-14.
